title: Graham's number makes googolplex look like zero
body: While solving a Ramsey theory problem, Ronald Graham needed a bound so large that Knuth invented arrow notation just to write it; ordinary exponent towers overflow any page. Graham's number ends in a known last digit, 7, despite being unwriteable in full. It entered pop culture as the benchmark for finite-but-unimaginable.
source_hint: Graham and Rothschild (1971); Knuth up-arrow notation
